Amazon.A value is: a scalar copied onto the item, inside an array-of-objects envelope: [{value, marketplace_id, language_tag}]; whether Flavor / flavor.value_id / Flavor Standardized Values are three attributes or one is not established (U16).
Amazon.Allowed list lives on: the per-(ProductType, marketplace) schema — a soft enum: a free string is schema-valid, a suggested closed list sits alongside; enum/enumNames display values vs the validator's undocumented snake_case codes (Amazon staff: “a valid concern”).
Amazon.A quantity is: five shapes in one schema: {value, unit}, unit_count {value, type}, a bare integer, free-text size ≤50 chars, and text.
Amazon.Picker order comes from: the enum array's own order (enumNames “in the same order as the values in the enum array”); no position field.
Amazon.Example:
● 
"item_weight": [{"value": 4, "marketplace_id": "ATVPDKIKX0DER"}]
"flavor":      [{"value": "Chocolate", "marketplace_id": "ATVPDKIKX0DER", "language_tag": "en_US"}]
(#10976 §1.3; second line ◇ from the same envelope)

Shopify.A value is: hybrid by option kind: an unlinked option value is a string on the product (600 products → 600 distinct ProductOptionValue ids for one name); a linked value carries linkedMetafieldValue: gid://shopify/Metaobject/…, a row many products share. Metafield values are always stored as strings.
Shopify.Allowed list lives on: taxonomy: the attribute (a TaxonomyValue belongs to exactly one, 0 of 74,820 shared); linked options: the metafield definition constrained by category; unlinked: the product.
Shopify.A quantity is: weight and unit price on the variant (inventoryItem.measurement.weight {value: Float!, unit}); the taxonomy's TaxonomyMeasurementAttribute.options are bare {key, value: String} — 0 instances on 16 categories live, 0 of 383 in the corpus.
Shopify.Picker order comes from: per-product option values: array order via productOptionsReorder (“The order of values within each option determines their new positions”); the shared taxonomy list: sort_by_localized_name, Other pinned last (custom order on 7 of 8,240).

Google.A value is: a string on the product; four open layers — ProductDetail {sectionName ≤140, attributeName ≤140, attributeValue ≤1000} (≤100) · CustomAttribute {name, value} (≤2,500) · VariantOption {name ≤250, value ≤250} (≤30) · CloudExportAdditionalProperties; one typed layer of 145.
Google.Allowed list lives on: nowhere — flavour is only a suggested key name in product_detail (“not a comprehensive or exhaustive list”).
Google.A quantity is: text: “Value + unit” packed in one feed string; unit_pricing_measure / unit_pricing_base_measure beside it; no net-content field.

eBay.A value is: a string, copied per SKU — aspects: {name: [strings]}; no value id anywhere (valueId 0, aspectValueId 0).
eBay.Allowed list lives on: the leaf category's constraint — aspectValues[] {localizedValue, valueConstraints} when aspectMode = SELECTION_ONLY; FREE_TEXT on 156,337 of 197,046.
eBay.A quantity is: typed on the constraint only (aspectDataType NUMBER 482 / DATE 15; aspectFormat int32/double); every value is still a string; gap pass: Item Weight suggested values are label+unit strings ("250 g").
eBay.Picker order comes from: array order of aspectValues, no position field, no stated rule (Brand: Unbranded, Handmade, then alphabetical).
eBay.Example:
● 
"aspects": {"Color": ["Blue"], "Size": ["S"]}   — write side
"aspectValues": [{"localizedValue": "100 g"}, {"localizedValue": "1 kg"}, {"localizedValue": "250 g"}]  — Item Weight on leaf 257998
(#11045 §2; gap pass 2026-09-21)

Walmart.A value is: a string (or number) inline on the member, typed by the slot's JSON Schema; shared values are shared by repetition.
Walmart.Allowed list lives on: the product type's slot ("Closed List - …" + enum); for flavor all 385 declarations are type: string, maxLength 600, no enum.
Walmart.A quantity is: {unit, measure} objects on values like netContent; the axis-eligible size stays a free string.
Walmart.Picker order comes from: a per-type ranked list of variant attributes that is “published nowhere”.

Shopee.A value is: a shared row by id — value_id int32 required — or the sentinel value_id: 0 + original_value_name (free text).
Shopee.Allowed list lives on: the attribute — search_attribute_value_list keyed by attribute_id alone; attribute_value_list[] {value_id, name, value_unit, child_attribute_list}.
Shopee.A quantity is: typed with a unit when format_type = 2: name = “5kg”, value_unit = the unit from attribute_unit_list; variation options are bare labels.

Tokopedia.A value is: Era A: a row per variant unit — VariantUnitValue {variant_unit_value_id int, status, value string, equivalent_value_id, english_value, hex, icon}, with a free-text escape (“fill value”). Era B: {id, name} for product attributes, {id, value_id, value_name, name} for sales attributes — id-bearing row or a name.
Tokopedia.Allowed list lives on: the attribute (values[] {id, name, icon_url}; built-in value ids).
Tokopedia.A quantity is: Era A: none. Era B: skus.sku_unit_count: string paired with “base unit count” and “unit type” product attributes; “Unit price = Selling price / (SKU unit count / base unit count)”; all money/quantity fields strings.
Tokopedia.Picker order comes from: Era A: sort_order on the Annotation group; Era B: not stated.

Square.A value is: an option value: a shared row by id — the variation stores {item_option_id, item_option_value_id}; a custom-attribute value: inline (string_value / number_value / boolean_value / selection_uid_values).
Square.Allowed list lives on: the option (CatalogItemOption.values) — reusable across items; “If the seller later receives teal polo shirts, they must add ‘Teal’ to the color option set.”
Square.A quantity is: a unit on the variation via measurement_unit_id → CatalogMeasurementUnit.
Square.Picker order comes from: a stored position on the value: CatalogItemOptionValue.ordinal: int32 (“Determines where this option value appears”); vendor's response shows 6, 7, 8, 9.

Salesforce B2C.A value is: @value — NonEmptyString.256, 1..1 required (red, 1 GB) + <display-value> localized 0..N + position; local vs shared is first-class (variation-attribute inline vs shared-variation-attribute reference; shared: boolean).
Salesforce B2C.Allowed list lives on: the definition (ENUM_OF_STRING) or the variation attribute (post-migration).
Salesforce B2C.A quantity is: one opaque string (1 GB); unit: String on the definition, unit-quantity xsd:decimal + unit-measure on the product.
Salesforce B2C.Example:
◇ 
<variation-attribute-value value="1 GB"><display-value xml:lang="x-default">1 GB</display-value></variation-attribute-value>
— the XSD shape; no instance data (U9)

Akeneo.A value is: a shared row at the definition (pim_catalog_attribute_option UNIQUE (code, attribute_id), labels per locale in pim_catalog_attribute_option_value) — but the product copies the option code as a string in raw_values; integrity is a case-insensitive validator, not an FK.
Akeneo.Allowed list lives on: the attribute — AttributeOption.attribute manyToOne exactly 1; no family/category field.
Akeneo.A quantity is: pim_catalog_metric = {amount, unit} on the value from a shared unit registry; the definition carries metric_family, default_metric_unit, decimals_allowed, negative_allowed; axis-eligible.
Akeneo.Picker order comes from: sort_order by default, or alphabetical by translated label when auto_option_sorting is on — “drag and drop option rows to reorder”.

WooCommerce.A value is: a term for the attribute (“a bare label — id, name, slug, description, menu_order, count”, shared across products) — but the variation stores its axis value as a copied slug string, always (update_post_meta($id, 'attribute_' . $key, $value)).
WooCommerce.Allowed list lives on: the attribute (global terms) or the product (local attributes, “only exist for that single product”).
WooCommerce.A quantity is: nothing — six bare fields; numeric sort is an ORDER BY t.name+0 hack.
WooCommerce.Picker order comes from: attribute_orderby ∈ menu_order | name | name_num | id (default menu_order; name_num measured broken on S, M, L, XL, Red, 2…).
WooCommerce.Example:
● 
term: {term_id: 27, name: "Mint", slug: "mint", menu_order: 0}   variation 27: attribute_pa_flavour = 'mint'
(#11080 §1.5, §2 step 6)

commercetools.A value is: Attribute {name, value: any} on the variant; an enum value is AttributePlainEnumValue {key, label} nested in the ProductType document, not an addressable row (the record withdrew its own “copied” reading).
commercetools.Allowed list lives on: the definition, per ProductType — “the enum values can be different for each ProductType”.
commercetools.A quantity is: typed, no physical unit — 13 types (number, money with currency); 0 unit fields.
commercetools.Picker order comes from: the enum array; changePlainEnumValueOrder update action (corroborated in the corpus).

Magento.A value is: a shared row referenced by an integer — catalog_product_entity_int.value = option_id; the label is fanned out per store view, never per product.
Magento.Allowed list lives on: the attribute — eav_attribute_option (option_id, attribute_id, sort_order) → eav_attribute_option_value (value_id, option_id, store_id, value varchar(255)), UNIQUE (store_id, option_id).
Magento.A quantity is: nothing — 0 unit fields across 67 schema files (control 12); decimal backend type only.
Magento.Example:
● configurable/93/53 — option 53 referenced on two surfaces of one response; ◇ 
eav_attribute_option       {option_id: 53, attribute_id: 83, sort_order: 2}
eav_attribute_option_value {option_id: 53, store_id: 0, value: 'Red'}
